Third-party source, vendored and committed
==========================================

WHY THESE ARE COMMITTED WHEN imgui AND minhook ARE NOT

imgui\ and minhook\ are cloned at build time (see build.bat and the README's
build section). They are fifty-odd files each, actively developed, and they draw
the panel and patch a vtable -- if either is the wrong version the failure is
loud and immediate.

These are different in the respects that matter. They are effectively frozen,
and they sit on the path where a .wrpath's contents are decided. A decompressor
that is subtly the wrong version does not fail loudly; it produces a slightly
different byte somewhere in a run and the line in the world bends the wrong way.
Committing them makes git the pin, and makes "what exactly is in this build" a
question with one answer.

Not "two or three files" any more, which is what this paragraph used to say.
zstd's decompression half is thirty of them, and that entry argues the cost
rather than glossing it -- the alternative was a one-file decoder that calls
exit(1) on malformed input, inside a game.

Nothing here is modified. Every file is byte-for-byte what upstream published,
which is the point -- a reviewer can diff against the release and be done. If
one of them ever HAS to be patched, the patch goes in a .diff beside it and gets
named here, rather than being edited in place where nobody would find it.

The build compiles them on their own cl line, as C, with the options below. It
never includes them from a header of ours: only the .cpp that needs one includes
it, so the surface stays where you can see it.


miniz 3.1.2
-----------
what     zlib inflate. Momentum's map catalogue (momentum\_cache\*.dat) is a
         12-byte header and then a raw zlib stream, and reading it is what lets
         the Maps tab list every map without asking anybody's server.
upstream https://github.com/richgel999/miniz
release  https://github.com/richgel999/miniz/releases/tag/3.1.2
archive  miniz-3.1.2.zip
         sha256 f0446d863f9c19926ad9483c523fdc42e42b8d4a6a431d27e09d49c79a140d9a
         101958 bytes
licence  MIT. See miniz\LICENSE.
vendored 2026-08-10
files    miniz.c, miniz.h, LICENSE. The examples\, readme and ChangeLog from the
         release archive are not here.
used     tinfl_decompress_mem_to_heap() with TINFL_FLAG_PARSE_ZLIB_HEADER, and
         mz_free(). That is the whole of it -- see src\wr_msml.cpp.

compiled out, and why each one:
  MINIZ_NO_ARCHIVE_APIS           the .zip reader. We never open an archive, and
                                  it is the part of miniz with a CVE history.
                                  (This also switches off the archive WRITING
                                  apis on its own, so passing that one as well
                                  is a redefinition warning rather than belt and
                                  braces.)
  MINIZ_NO_DEFLATE_APIS           we only ever decompress. Note this is why the
                                  test fixtures carry pre-compressed bytes: this
                                  build genuinely cannot make a zlib stream.
  MINIZ_NO_STDIO                  no file handling; we hand it a buffer.
  MINIZ_NO_TIME                   only the archive code wants a clock.
  MINIZ_NO_ZLIB_COMPATIBLE_NAMES  keeps bare compress/uncompress/crc32 out of
                                  the link. wrlines.dll exports nothing and the
                                  build asserts that; this is the same instinct
                                  applied to the symbols going in.


LZMA SDK 23.01
--------------
what     the LZMA1 decoder. A Momentum demo's run body is a raw LZMA1 stream
         behind a seventeen-byte Valve header, and it is the only thing between
         a .mtv on disk and any of the numbers this program draws.
upstream https://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html
release  https://www.7-zip.org/a/lzma2301.7z  (dated 2023-06-20)
archive  lzma2301.7z
         sha256 317dd834d6bbfd95433488b832e823cd3d4d420101436422c03af88507dd1370
         1322733 bytes
licence  public domain. See lzma\LICENSE, under the heading LICENSE -- that file
         is DOC\lzma-sdk.txt from the archive, unmodified, renamed so that a
         reader looking for the licence finds it where they expect to.
vendored 2026-08-10
files    LzmaDec.c, LzmaDec.h, 7zTypes.h, Precomp.h, Compiler.h. That is not a
         judgement call: DOC\lzma.txt names exactly those five as what an
         ANSI-C decoder needs, and the archive's other four hundred files are
         the encoder, LZMA2, XZ, 7z, C++, C# and Java.
         sha256, in the same order:
           0b938edae2aec133d144e2ff3493ac2b82850b3bbf8a79d1e925409124d39933
           3a3b0ece1ba58601a8265a421a91b9720b39ee92ce898fadecb22f052bc3011f
           1cd69ecb9e6cf97949aca3faa53ecd7590149efade07c6f816e9bb48515b2329
           87a4dcb75ec1a24b7d77ec82d90499f276d14c401a1fa3841f9d9986c285efe8
           a7ab2e9b059c6830280fc63c8a8f5254b48b847a0701f73bea409f954134852e
used     LzmaDecode(), the one-call interface, and nothing else. See
         src\wr_mtv.cpp.

         Worth knowing, because it decided how much of this file there needed
         to be: LzmaDecode() decompresses straight into the destination buffer
         and the allocator it is handed is used only for the probability model
         -- a few hundred kilobytes, fixed. The dictionary size in the stream's
         own property bytes therefore allocates nothing, so a demo claiming a
         four-gigabyte dictionary is not a thing that has to be clamped. It is
         only a bound on match distances, which the decoder already checks
         against how much output exists.

compiled out
         nothing, and that is the answer rather than an omission. The usual
         flag to reach for is _7ZIP_ST, "no threading layer" -- but in 23.01
         the block that acts on it is commented out in 7zTypes.h, and none of
         the other four files mentions it. Passing it would have looked like
         due diligence and done nothing at all, which is worse than not
         passing it. These five files include only <errno.h>, <stddef.h>,
         <stdint.h> and <string.h>, and pull in no Windows header.


zstd 1.5.7, decompression only
------------------------------
what     the zstd decoder. About 5% of the demos in a Momentum install have a
         zstd run body rather than a Valve-LZMA one, and among the demos this
         tool DOWNLOADS from the leaderboard it is 7.7% -- on surf_tropic, 50
         of 100. They are the long runs, which is the same observation twice.
         Until v0.9.4 they were recognised and refused; see src\wr_mtv.h.
upstream https://github.com/facebook/zstd
release  https://github.com/facebook/zstd/releases/tag/v1.5.7
archive  zstd-1.5.7.tar.gz
         sha256 eb33e51f49a15e023950cd7825ca74a4a2b43db8354825ac24fc1b7ee09e6fa3
         2434947 bytes
licence  BSD-3-Clause, or GPLv2 at your option. Both texts are here: LICENSE is
         the BSD one and COPYING the GPL, which is how upstream ships them. This
         project takes the BSD option.
vendored 2026-08-15
used     ZSTD_getFrameContentSize(), ZSTD_decompress(), ZSTD_isError() and
         ZSTD_getErrorName(). That is the whole of it -- see src\wr_mtv.cpp.

WHY THIRTY FILES WHERE LZMA NEEDS FIVE

         This is by far the largest thing in this directory and the choice was
         made twice, so the reasoning is worth having.

         zstd publishes a second decoder: doc\educational_decoder, one .c and
         one .h, fifteen hundred lines, complete for the format. It is exactly
         what the rule at the top of this file wants -- small, frozen, one file
         to diff. It is also unusable here, and its own comments say why:

             /// This decoder calls exit(1) when it encounters an error,
             /// however a production library should propagate error codes

         Roughly thirty call sites. Inside momentum.exe that is the game
         closing, with no message, because somebody's demo was truncated on the
         way down from a CDN. And these bodies DO arrive over the network -- the
         quick menu downloads them -- so malformed input is a case that has to
         return, not a case that cannot happen. Compiling it with exit
         redefined to a longjmp was considered and rejected: it leaves a
         reference implementation, one that says of itself that it is not
         hardened, parsing bytes this program did not produce.

         So: lib\decompress plus the part of lib\common it needs, which is what
         every program that ships zstd links, is fuzzed continuously by
         OSS-Fuzz, and returns error codes. The cost is this file list.

         NOT vendored, and each is deliberate: lib\compress (nothing here ever
         compresses), lib\dictBuilder, lib\deprecated, lib\legacy (see
         ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT below), programs\, and
         decompress\huf_decompress_amd64.S -- assembly needs ml64.exe in the
         build, and ZSTD_DISABLE_ASM selects the C path that is there for
         exactly this. pool.c and threading.c are absent because nothing in the
         decompression path includes them; that was checked rather than assumed.

compiled out
         ZSTD_DISABLE_ASM=1     the amd64 Huffman assembly, which is not
                                vendored. This is the load-bearing one: without
                                it the build asks for a .S file that is not
                                there.
         ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT=0  readers for zstd frame formats v0.1 through
                                v0.7, none of which any demo uses -- the format
                                was stable years before Momentum existed. It is
                                also 0 by default in this layout; passing it is
                                a lock rather than a change.
         ZSTD_MULTITHREAD=0     the worker pool. Decompression does not use one,
                                and this file's own pool (wr_jobs.h) is what
                                runs demos in parallel. Keeps pool.c and
                                threading.c out of the link.
         ZSTD_NO_TRACE=1        the tracing hooks, which are weak symbols for a
                                profiler that is not here.

files    thirty, and their sha256, in the order `find | sort` gives them:

         `tar xf zstd-1.5.7.tar.gz` and a diff of the two trees. Nothing is
         modified; there is no .diff beside any of them.
